approach:
Root cause: the scope guard flattens each finished attempt to a verdict, a cost and minutes (`AttemptRecord`, scope_guard.rs:102-119, built in `attempt_of` at :606). T3 then treats spend as one number (`t3_cost`, :321-335), so it cannot tell a rejection one named gap short from one that got nowhere. Environment stops are already handled in one place (`verdict_of`, :561-573, calls `crate::disk::is_environment_reason`). This change leaves that alone and adds no second list.

The change adds the missing fact where the attempt is built. `AttemptRecord` gains `progress: Option<Progress>`, with `Progress { met, total, bounded }`. `attempt_of` fills it from the job's stored `Verification` only when the verdict is Rejected. Failed, Environment and Accepted attempts carry None.

`bounded` is true only when the unmet criteria are all that rejected the attempt. It is read from structured fields, never from reason text. Round-2 finding 1 is answered by counting Major findings by source:
1. `agent_verdict` is Some, and the verifier's invocation (`Verification.verifier_invocation` is its `seq`) is recorded in `job.invocations` with outcome Success. This removes the old "incomplete verifier" limit, because `verdict_output` is kept even when the verifier did not finish (run/verification.rs:275-294).
2. `request_reading_mismatch` is None.
3. No finding of any source is a Blocker.
4. Verifier-sourced Majors number no more than the unmet criteria. The verifier is told to rate an unmet criterion Major (verifier.md:9).
5. Athena-sourced Majors number no more than `judged_gaps`. `judged_gaps` counts the criteria with `!commands_verified && (kind == Behavior || commands.is_empty())`. `judge` pushes exactly one Athena Major for each of those and no other per-criterion Major. A behavior criterion with no seen command gets one (verify.rs:586-604). An unassessed criterion gets one (verify.rs:549-555), with empty commands and `commands_verified` false. Any other Athena Major is unrelated to a criterion and makes the attempt unbounded. Examples are a requirement row marked Covered (verify.rs:492-499) and the replay Blocker (:501-531).
6. Every failed check is pre-existing or a revert run. The filter is the one at gate_counts.rs:64-76: `!passed`, `revert_for` empty, and note not starting with PRE_EXISTING_NOTE. `mark_pre_existing` stores the note before the verification is written (run/mod.rs:2161).

`pub fn near_complete(&AttemptRecord)` is true for a Rejected attempt with bounded progress, met below total, and met/total at least `NEAR_COMPLETE_SHARE = 0.8`, an estimate marked as such.

`t3_cost` keeps its arithmetic in a private `t3_by_spend`. It returns Flag instead of Pause when that level is Pause and `targeted_retry(attempts, forecast)` holds. This is the exact rule for round-2 finding 2. The last counted attempt must be near-complete, and it must not be the second near-complete one in a row with the line's spend already at the pause limit at the earlier one. In code, `counted_at` yields the non-environment attempts with their indices. If the counted attempt before the last is near-complete, `targeted_retry` evaluates `t3_by_spend` on `attempts[..=that index]` and the allowance is spent when that is Pause. So the first time T3 crosses the pause limit on a near-complete rejection, the line is flagged and gets one targeted retry. A second near-complete rejection straight after, with spend still over the limit, pauses through T3 itself. An earlier near-complete attempt under the limit does not use the allowance, and an environment stop between two attempts neither resets nor uses it. T1, T2, T4 and T5 are untouched.

`line_state` (scope_guard.rs:735-744) is the one path to `t3_cost`, so `line_pause`, `line_flag`, `live_marks` and the watcher all follow the new rule. `facts` appends a clause to the T3 detail of a newly written flag when the pause was withheld. The condition needs no `targeted_retry` call: T3 is Flag while spend is at least 1.5 times a positive forecast, and only the downgrade can give that. No stored shape changes (`LineMark`, `MarkNumbers`, `SignalFact`).

A pause stored before this change on a near-complete line is no longer returned by `line_pause`, so go, retry and the drain are not refused. The line shows no flag until its next attempt finishes (the watcher removed the flag file when it wrote the pause, :1074-1076, and `line_flag` reads only the flag file, :842). The plan says so in the changelog and pins it with a test. It does not change `line_flag`, because the existing test at :1820-1823 pins that a pause mark is not a flag.

Doc comments on `AttemptRecord`, `t3_cost` and the module header name the root cause and say environment stops stay excluded through `crate::disk::is_environment_reason` with no second list. `status.rs`, `drain.rs` and `disk.rs` get doc-only edits. `CHANGELOG.md` gets one entry. No refusal or matching rule is added and reading.rs is not touched, so 0% of past accepted readings are refused and no refusal-corpus case applies.

decisions.choice: Carry `Progress { met, total, bounded }` on AttemptRecord. attempt_of sets it for Rejected only. `bounded` is computed from the stored Verification by one private function, `gaps_only`, which counts Majors by source: verifier-sourced Majors at most the unmet criteria, Athena-sourced Majors at most `judged_gaps` (criteria with `!commands_verified && (kind == Behavior || commands.is_empty())`), and no Blocker.
decisions.reason: This answers round-2 finding 1. `judge` pushes an Athena Major for a behavior criterion whose cited commands were not seen (verify.rs:586-604) and for an unassessed criterion (verify.rs:550-554), and the verifier also rates the same gap Major (verifier.md:9). Two Majors for one gap is therefore the usual shape for behavior criteria, and a plain count of all Majors would bring the old pause back for them. An unrelated Athena Major, such as a requirement row marked Covered (verify.rs:492-499) or the replay Blocker (:501-531), must not hide behind an unmet criterion. `Finding.source` (records.rs:271-276) and `CriterionResult.commands`, `commands_verified` and `kind` (records.rs:911-919) separate the two. `judged_gaps` mirrors `judge` exactly: a content criterion with a cited command that was not seen has `commands_verified` false but gets no Athena Major, because only Behavior criteria are marked unmet by Athena (verify.rs:586). So the critic's looser rule, a count of `commands_verified == false`, could let an unrelated Athena Major through next to such a criterion. A test builds its records with the real `crate::verify::judge`, so a change in `judge` breaks the test instead of silently drifting. AttemptRecord is built in three places only (scope_guard.rs:606, the test helper `att` at 2092, and `..att` at 2435), and a grep of the repository finds no other file that names it.

rejected.option: Count Major findings against unmet criteria, all sources together (round-2 plan)
rejected.why: Round-2 finding 1: one behavior gap yields an Athena Major and a verifier Major, so 2 is more than 1 and the pause returns for the usual criterion kind. In the other direction, one unmet content criterion plus an unrelated Athena Major reads as bounded.

rejected.option: Athena-sourced Majors at most the count of criteria with `commands_verified == false`
rejected.why: A content criterion with an unseen cited command has `commands_verified` false and no Athena Major (verify.rs:583-586), so this count can hide an unrelated Athena Major. The tighter `judged_gaps` predicate matches what `judge` produces.

rejected.option: Read `Verification.reasons` text to find other causes
rejected.why: The strings are free text in verify.rs:450, 476, 628 and 647-657 with no shared constants. A second parser would break when the wording changes. The structured fields carry the same facts.

rejected.option: Store only met and total and decide near-completeness from the share (round-1 plan)
rejected.why: verify.rs:627-664 rejects for a misread, a Blocker or Major finding, or a failing check whatever the criteria say, so 8 of 9 met would hide each of those.

rejected.option: Only change t3_basis to drop the spend of rejected attempts that kept a candidate
rejected.why: A rejected candidate is not an environment stop. Dropping its spend would hide runaway spend on a line that is nowhere near done.

rejected.option: Add a stop-reason enum or a second list of environment reasons on AttemptRecord
rejected.why: crate::disk::StopCause (disk.rs:428-443) is the one classifier. A second list is what caused the earlier expired-login pause (scope_guard.rs:19-24).

decisions.choice: Read the verifier's own run outcome as part of `bounded`: the Verification's `verifier_invocation` seq must match an `Invocation` of role Verifier in `job.invocations` with `outcome == InvocationOutcome::Success`. Without such a record, the attempt is not bounded.
decisions.reason: A verifier that did not finish still leaves parsed output: `verdict_output` is set from `voutput.structured` whatever the outcome (run/verification.rs:277-294), and `verifier_invocation` is set before that (:275). The failure itself is not stored as a field, only as reason text. The invocation record carries the outcome as a structured value (records.rs:749-768, InvocationOutcome 134-143). This removes the 'verifier incomplete but returned output' limit that the round-2 plan had to state. A missing record falls back to unbounded, which is the old behaviour, so the rule relaxes the pause only on positive evidence.

rejected.option: State it as a known limit in the changelog (round-2 plan)
rejected.why: The structured fact exists in the same job's records and costs a few lines to read.

decisions.choice: Downgrade only T3, from Pause to Flag. `targeted_retry(attempts, forecast)` holds when the last counted attempt is near_complete and NOT (the counted attempt before it is also near_complete and `t3_by_spend` of the attempts up to that one is already Pause). Counted attempts come from a new `counted_at`, which keeps the index and has the same filter as `counted()` (scope_guard.rs:245-250).
decisions.reason: This answers round-2 finding 2 by changing the rule, not only the docs, so the code does what the changelog says: the first time T3 trips on a near-complete rejection the line gets one targeted retry. Under the round-2 rule ('last is near, the one before is not'), a line [near under the limit, near over the limit] paused at once and never got the retry, and after a lifted pause [near, Failed, near] downgraded again. Under this rule the allowance is used only when a downgrade was actually possible at the earlier attempt. [3 of 9 over the limit, then 8 of 9] still flags: the line shows convergence after a lift. [near over, near over] pauses through T3. T4 pauses only on the same criterion twice (:338-360) and T5 only at 120 minutes (:371-385), so without this limit near-complete rejections that each miss a different criterion would spend with no T3 stop.

rejected.option: Keep the round-2 rule and say 'two in a row' in the docs (the critic's first alternative)
rejected.why: The allowance would still be lost to an attempt that never tripped T3, so the line would pause on its first trip with no retry, which is the case the request wants to avoid.

rejected.option: Unlimited downgrade while the last attempt is near-complete (round-1 plan)
rejected.why: Round-1 finding: only T5 would stop it, and only at 120 minutes.

rejected.option: A second ceiling such as 2 times T3_PAUSE_RATIO times the forecast
rejected.why: It adds a second magic number and says nothing about progress. The once-per-trip rule uses the progress fact this change already carries.

rejected.option: Clear T3 entirely (Level::None) for a near-complete attempt
rejected.why: A flag keeps the spend visible in status and lets the drain pass the item over after two failures (drain.rs:47-52).

decisions.choice: NEAR_COMPLETE_SHARE is the const 0.8, tested as met < total and f64::from(met) / f64::from(total) >= 0.8. The doc comment marks it an estimate and a judgement call, and says it is a share of criteria met, not of effort.
decisions.reason: It is the 80% of the accepted reading. 8 of 9 (0.889) and 4 of 5 (exactly 0.8) pass, and 7 of 9 (0.778) does not. Every threshold in the module is an estimate to be tuned (scope_guard.rs:26).

rejected.why: It hides the named constant that the doc comments and the changelog cite.

decisions.choice: Do not change line_flag or live_marks for a pause stored before the change. State the unflagged gap in the changelog and the t3_cost doc, and pin it with a test (B3).
decisions.reason: line_flag returns a mark only from the flag file (scope_guard.rs:842), and the existing test at 1820-1823 requires that a stored pause is not a flag. The gap closes by itself: the watcher writes the flag after the next attempt (:1083), and the drain asks line_flag only after an item's failed attempt (drain.rs:4429), by which time the watcher has run.

rejected.option: Let line_flag and live_marks return a stored pause whose recomputed level is Flag, shown as a flag
rejected.why: It breaks the pinned contract at :1820-1823, changes the displayed level of a mark, and widens the change to cover a window that closes by itself.

decisions.choice: Add no field to MarkNumbers, LineMark or SignalFact. `facts` appends a text clause to the T3 detail only when signals.t3 is Flag, the forecast in `numbers` is positive and `numbers.spend_usd >= T3_PAUSE_RATIO * numbers.forecast_p90_usd`.
decisions.reason: Marks are serialised under <state root>/scope/ and read with serde (scope_guard.rs:432-478, 511-513), and read_mark returns None for an unreadable file. A new required field would hide stored marks. The condition is exact without calling `targeted_retry`: t3_by_spend returns Pause at that spend, so a Flag there can only come from the downgrade. The clause reads the figures from the last counted attempt's progress (for example 'met 4 of 5').

rejected.option: Add near_complete or progress counts to MarkNumbers with #[serde(default)]
rejected.why: It touches display.rs lines_section (display.rs:1087) and its test (display.rs:2842) for a figure the text can carry.

decisions.choice: Edit status.rs, drain.rs and disk.rs by doc comments only: `StatusView.lines` (status.rs:507-509), the flagged-line bullet in the drain.rs module header (:47-52) and `StopCause` (disk.rs:419-427).
decisions.reason: They read the guard only through live_marks, line_pause and line_flag (drain.rs:4414-4439) and StopCause, and all of them recompute through line_state, so none needs logic. These are the places where a reader learns what a T3 flag covers and where to look for why an attempt stopped.

rejected.option: Add drain logic that treats a near-complete rejection specially
rejected.why: The drain already asks the guard. A second rule in the drain would be a second source of the decision.

files.purpose: Add `Progress`, `AttemptRecord.progress`, `NEAR_COMPLETE_SHARE`, `counted_at`, `progress_of`, `gaps_only`, `pub fn near_complete` and private `targeted_retry`. Fill `progress` in `attempt_of` for Rejected only. Split the spend arithmetic of `t3_cost` into `t3_by_spend` and downgrade Pause to Flag when `targeted_retry` holds. Add the T3 detail clause in `facts`. Update the doc comments of AttemptRecord, t3_cost and the module header (root cause, is_environment_reason, no second list, the exact allowance rule, the stored-pause gap). Update `att`, add `near`, widen CRITERIA, add `criteria` to rig_build with `rig_with_criteria`, and add the new tests.

One new bullet at the top of `## [Unreleased]` / `### Changed`: root cause, the fix, the bounded-gap rule counted by finding source, the 0.8 estimate, the exact allowance rule, environment stops still excluded by is_environment_reason with no second list, T1, T2, T4 and T5 unchanged, the lifting of stored pauses and the unflagged gap, the limits, the design-doc follow-up, 'no refusal rule is added (0% of past accepted readings refused)', and the test commands. Check it against boundary_words() (xtask/tests/policy.rs:88-113).
Doc comment only, on `StatusView.lines` (status.rs:507-509): a T3 mark there may be a flag for a near-complete line, and a stale pause is not shown. No logic change.

Doc comment only, in the module header bullet about a flagged line (drain.rs:47-52): a T3 flag can mean a near-complete rejection over the spend limit, so the item gets its second attempt and is passed over after two failures. No logic change.

Doc comment only, on `StopCause` (disk.rs:419-427): a rejection that got most of the way is not a stop cause; the guard reads it from the verification in `scope_guard::near_complete`. Environment stops are classified here only. No logic change.

steps: In crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs, import `CriterionKind`, `FindingSource`, `InvocationOutcome`, `PRE_EXISTING_NOTE`, `Severity` and `Verification` from athena_data::records. Do not import records' `Verdict`, which would clash with the module's own `Verdict`. Add `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct Progress { pub met: u32, pub total: u32, pub bounded: bool }` with docs. Add `pub progress: Option<Progress>` to AttemptRecord after `resumed`. Add `pub const NEAR_COMPLETE_SHARE: f64 = 0.8;` with a doc comment saying it is an estimate and a judgement call, a share of criteria not of effort. Rewrite the AttemptRecord doc to name the root cause (the guard treated every attempt's spend as one number and did not record how far a rejected attempt got), say `progress` is set only for a Rejected attempt with a verification record, and say environment stops stay excluded through crate::disk::is_environment_reason via `verdict_of`, with no second list. Add one sentence to the module header paragraph at lines 19-24 for the progress fact.

Add `fn counted_at(attempts) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = (usize, &AttemptRecord)>`, the enumerate-and-filter of `a.verdict != Verdict::Environment`, and rewrite `counted()` (:245) as `counted_at(attempts).map(|(_, a)| a).collect()`, so the environment filter has one definition.

Add `fn progress_of(job: &JobRecords) -> Option<Progress>`: None when there is no verification or its `criteria` is empty; otherwise `met` is the count of `c.met`, `total` is the length, and `bounded` comes from private `gaps_only(job, v)`. `gaps_only` is true only when all of these hold. (1) `v.agent_verdict.is_some()`. (2) `v.verifier_invocation` is Some(seq) and `job.invocations` holds an Invocation with `role == Role::Verifier`, that `seq` and `outcome == InvocationOutcome::Success`. (3) `v.request_reading_mismatch.is_none()`. (4) No finding has `Severity::Blocker`. (5) The Major findings with `source == FindingSource::Verifier` number at most `unmet` (the criteria with `!met`). (6) The Major findings with `source == FindingSource::Athena` number at most `judged_gaps`, the count of criteria with `!c.commands_verified && (c.kind == CriterionKind::Behavior || c.commands.is_empty())`. A comment cites verify.rs:549-555 and :586-604 as the source of that predicate. (7) Every check with `!passed` has a non-empty `revert_for` or a note that starts with PRE_EXISTING_NOTE (the filter at gate_counts.rs:64-76).

Add `pub fn near_complete(a: &AttemptRecord) -> bool`: the verdict is Rejected and the progress is Some, bounded, `total > 0`, `met < total` and `f64::from(met) / f64::from(total) >= NEAR_COMPLETE_SHARE`. Add private `fn targeted_retry(attempts: &[AttemptRecord], forecast_p90_dollars: f64) -> bool`: take `counted_at(attempts).rev()`; return false unless the last is near_complete; then, if the counted attempt before it exists and is near_complete with index `i`, return `t3_by_spend(&attempts[..=i], forecast_p90_dollars) != Level::Pause`; otherwise return true. Move the body of `t3_cost` (:321-335) into private `t3_by_spend`; make `t3_cost` call it and return `Level::Flag` when the result is Pause and `targeted_retry(attempts, forecast_p90_dollars)` holds. Rewrite the `t3_cost` doc: name the root cause; state the allowance exactly (a near-complete last attempt flags instead of pausing, unless the counted attempt before it was also near-complete and spend was already at the pause limit at that attempt, so the second near-complete rejection in a row over the limit pauses); say that spend of environment stops is excluded only through `t3_basis` and crate::disk::is_environment_reason with no second list; and say a pause stored earlier lifts by recompute and the line shows no flag until its next attempt.
In `attempt_of` (:580-615), set `progress` in the struct literal at :606 to `progress_of(job)` when `verdict == Verdict::Rejected`, and to None otherwise (Failed, Environment, Accepted, unlanded).

In `facts` (:746), extend the T3 detail: when `signals.t3 == Level::Flag`, `numbers.forecast_p90_usd > 0.0` and `numbers.spend_usd >= T3_PAUSE_RATIO * numbers.forecast_p90_usd`, append a clause built from the last counted attempt's progress: '; the last attempt met M of N criteria and nothing else rejected it, so the pause is withheld for one targeted retry'. Do not change LineMark, MarkNumbers or SignalFact.

Doc-only edits. In disk.rs, extend the StopCause doc (:419-427) with a sentence saying a near-complete rejection is not a stop cause, is read from the verification in `scope_guard::near_complete`, and that environment stops are classified here only. In drain.rs, extend the module header bullet at :47-52 with a clause: a T3 flag can mean a near-complete rejection over the spend limit, so its item gets the second attempt and is passed over after two failures. In status.rs, extend the doc of `lines` (:507-509) with one clause that a T3 mark may be a flag and a stale pause is not shown. Use plain backticks for names not in scope.

In `mod tests`: add `progress: None` to `att` (:2091); add helper `near(met, total, cost)` (a Rejected attempt with a bounded `Progress` and a criterion text). Add `a_near_complete_rejection_does_not_pause_t3`, `near_complete_targeted_retry_is_used_once_when_over_the_limit`, `near_complete_rejections_still_pause_through_t4_and_t5` and `near_complete_t3_detail_says_why_no_pause` with the cases in demonstrations 1 (A1, A1b, A2, A3). Leave the bodies of `environment_stop_is_not_counted_but_a_rejection_is` and `every_kind_of_environment_stop_is_an_environment_attempt` unchanged.

In `mod watcher_tests`: widen `CRITERIA` to nine fixed content texts whose first two are unchanged (used also at :2030-2034). Add a `criteria: usize` parameter to `rig_build`, and pass 2 from `rig_with_space` and `rig_counting`. Build the reader's `acceptance_criteria`, the producer's `criteria_check` and the verifier's `criteria` from `CRITERIA[..criteria]`, with the verifier's `met` equal to `fail != Some(i)`. Add `rig_with_criteria(p90, cost, verdicts, criteria)`. Add `attempt_of_records_how_far_a_near_complete_rejection_got`, `near_complete_gap_is_bounded_only_by_findings_of_the_gap`, `a_near_complete_rejection_is_flagged_and_the_next_attempt_is_dispatched`, `a_second_near_complete_rejection_over_the_spend_limit_pauses` and `a_t3_pause_stored_before_the_change_for_a_near_complete_line_does_not_block`, as in demonstrations 1 and 2. In the judge-based test, use `crate::verify::{judge, VerdictInputs}` with `athena_context::outputs` literals and `Criterion { text, kind }`; build the CheckRun cases field by field as at status.rs:2662-2675. Run the new rig tests first, since a reading rule could refuse the 5-criteria fixture.

Add one bullet at the top of `### Changed` under `## [Unreleased]` in CHANGELOG.md, covering everything listed for it in the files table. Check it against the banned-word list in xtask/tests/policy.rs:88-113 and write no email-like text.
Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Fix any dead-code, doc-link or banned-word failure.

risks.risk: A line of near-complete rejections that each miss a different criterion spends with no T3 stop (round-1 finding 4).
risks.mitigation: The downgrade is spent when the counted attempt before the last was near-complete and the line was already at the pause limit at that attempt. The second near-complete rejection over 1.5 times the forecast pauses through T3 itself (test B2 and A1b). A Failed or less-complete last attempt pauses at once. T1, T2, T4 and T5 are unchanged. Cost: a line that needs two targeted retries over the limit is paused after the second, and the person running Athena lifts it by deleting the pause file.

risks.risk: `bounded` mis-ties findings to gaps. Findings carry no criterion index (records.rs:921-929), so verifier Majors are tied to unmet criteria by count: one unrelated verifier Major next to one unmet criterion with no Major of its own reads as bounded.
risks.mitigation: Athena-sourced Majors are tied through `judged_gaps`, which mirrors judge's own per-criterion findings, so an unrelated Athena Major, a Blocker, a misread, a failing check and an unfinished verifier all make the attempt unbounded (tested through the real judge). The residual count-based limit for verifier Majors is stated in the changelog. A line that reads as bounded wrongly is flagged and gets one more attempt, then pauses on the second near-complete rejection over the limit.

risks.risk: `gaps_only` drifts from `judge` if judge adds a new per-criterion Athena finding.
risks.mitigation: The new test builds its records with the real `crate::verify::judge`, so a change in what judge pushes for a criterion fails the test. An Athena Major that `judged_gaps` does not predict makes the attempt unbounded, so the failure direction is the old pause.

risks.risk: A pause stored before the change lifts by recompute, and the line has no flag until its next attempt finishes (round-1 finding 2). Status shows nothing for it in between.
risks.mitigation: Stated in the changelog and the t3_cost doc, and pinned by test B3. The next attempt's watcher writes the flag (scope_guard.rs:1083). The drain asks line_flag only after an item's failed attempt, after the watcher has run (drain.rs:47-52).

risks.risk: The 0.8 share is an estimate and criteria differ in weight. The effect on past lines was not measured because records/ is absent from the planning copy.
risks.mitigation: A named constant marked an estimate and a judgement call, like every threshold in the module (scope_guard.rs:26). The doc says it is a share of criteria met, not of effort, and the changelog says the effect on past lines was not measured. The rule only holds back a pause once per trip over the limit, and it never lowers T1, T2, T4 or T5.

risks.risk: The 5-criteria rig might be refused by a reading rule, or the fake producer's `criteria_check` might not match the verifier's texts.
risks.mitigation: CRITERIA is widened to nine fixed texts whose first two are unchanged, and the reader, producer and verifier JSON are built from the same `CRITERIA[..criteria]` slice, so the texts agree. No admission rule caps the count (admission.rs:184 reads it for planning only, which is off in the rig). The producer runs the new rig test first. If the reading is refused, it reports which rule in reading.rs refused it and does not loosen the rule.

risks.risk: Doc-only edits to status.rs, drain.rs and disk.rs could break rustdoc links or the banned-word scan.
risks.mitigation: Use plain backticks for names not in scope and write no word from boundary_words() (xtask/tests/policy.rs:88-113). `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` run the policy test.

dependents.name: t3_cost level (Pause becomes Flag for a near-complete last attempt, once per trip over the pause limit)
dependents.dependent: crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs: evaluate_before_attempt (:415) and line_state (:735-744), the one path to t3_cost. Callers of line_state: Athena::line_pause (:822), line_flag (:836), live_marks (:959) and try_watch_line (:1005). watch_line is called from crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:439 after each finished attempt. go refuses a paused line at run/mod.rs:1040 and retry at reading.rs:1280. demonstrations.method:
New tests whose names all contain `near_complete`, in two layers. (A) Pure unit tests in `mod tests` of crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs call `t3_cost` and `evaluate_before_attempt` on `AttemptRecord` lists. (B) Whole-path tests in `mod watcher_tests` drive `Athena::go` through `watch_line`, `line_state` and `line_pause` on the Rig, whose fake verifier judges 5 criteria.

Test A1 `a_near_complete_rejection_does_not_pause_t3` uses a forecast p90 of 2.0 throughout:
- one Rejected attempt, 8 of 9 met, cost 3.0 (1.5 times the forecast): `t3_cost` is below Pause (Flag).
- the same with 3 of 9: Pause.
- 7 of 9: Pause.
- 4 of 5: Flag (the 0.8 boundary).
- 9 of 9 with a Rejected verdict: Pause.
- 8 of 9 with bounded false: Pause.
- 8 of 9 with no progress: Pause.
- a Failed attempt that carries a progress value: Pause.
- [8 of 9, then 3 of 9] over the limit: Pause (the last attempt decides).
- [3 of 9, then 8 of 9] over the limit: Flag.
- [8 of 9, environment stop]: Flag (the stop is skipped).
- `evaluate_before_attempt` on the 8-of-9 line: t3 is Flag and overall is Flag.

Test A1b `near_complete_targeted_retry_is_used_once_when_over_the_limit` (finding 2):
- [8 of 9 at 0.5, 8 of 9 at 3.0]: Flag, because spend was under the limit at the earlier attempt, so the allowance is unused.
- [8 of 9 at 3.0, 8 of 9 at 0.1]: Pause.
- [8 of 9 at 3.0, 8 of 9 at 3.0, 8 of 9 at 0.1]: Pause.
- [8 of 9 at 3.0, Failed, 8 of 9 at 0.1]: Flag, because the counted attempt before is not near-complete.
- [8 of 9 at 3.0, environment stop, 8 of 9 at 0.1]: Pause, because the stop is skipped.

Test A2 `near_complete_rejections_still_pause_through_t4_and_t5`: two near-complete rejections of one criterion pause through T4 with a large forecast, and a near-complete attempt of 130 agent minutes pauses through T5.

Test A3 `near_complete_t3_detail_says_why_no_pause`: `facts` for the 8-of-9 line has a T3 flag whose detail names 'met 8 of 9' and says the pause was withheld. A flag at 1.0 times the forecast has no such clause.

B1 `a_near_complete_rejection_is_flagged_and_the_next_attempt_is_dispatched`: `rig_with_criteria(1.0, 0.8, &[Some(0), None], 5)`. `r.ask("describe the demo in the readme")` then `r.go` returns Rejected with 4 of 5 met and spend 1.6 against p90 1.0. Assert there is no pause file, and a flag file whose `signal_names()` is 'T3', whose spend is about 1.6 and whose reason contains 'met 4 of 5'. Assert `line_pause` is None. Then `r.ask("try again on <a>")` and `r.go` returns Landed (not refused).

B2 `a_second_near_complete_rejection_over_the_spend_limit_pauses` (round-1 finding 4): `rig_with_criteria(1.0, 0.8, &[Some(0), Some(1)], 5)` and `r.two_rejections()`. The second attempt's T4 is No (criteria 0 and 1 differ), T1 flags (3rd attempt next), and T3 is Pause (the earlier attempt was near-complete and already at 1.6 of a 1.5 limit). The pause file exists with a T3 fact at level pause, and `r.go` of a third retry returns an error whose text contains 'T3'.

B3 `a_t3_pause_stored_before_the_change_for_a_near_complete_line_does_not_block`: after the first rejection of B1, delete the flag file and write `write_mark(r.pause(&a), &mark("pause", a.as_str(), "T3"))`. `line_pause` is None. `line_flag` is None and `status().lines` is empty (the documented gap). `go` of the retry returns Landed.
demonstrations.observes: `t3_cost` returns Flag for 8 of 9 and for 4 of 5, and Pause for 3 of 9, 7 of 9, 9 of 9, unbounded, no progress, a Failed last attempt and a second consecutive near-complete rejection that is over the limit. The under-limit-then-over-limit sequence flags. On the real path, a near-complete line is flagged not paused and its retry runs. The second consecutive one pauses with T3. A stored old pause stops blocking.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base, `AttemptRecord` has no `progress` field, so the tests do not compile. If only the field were added and `t3_cost` left alone, `t3_cost(&[near(8,9,3.0)], 2.0)` returns Pause and the 'below Pause' assertion fails, and B1 would find a pause file and a refused `go` (run/mod.rs:1040). If the downgrade ignored the earlier attempt, the A1 and A1b over-the-limit sequences and B2 fail. If it ignored the spend at the earlier attempt, the under-then-over case fails. If it counted environment stops, the environment-stop sequences fail.

demonstrations.method:
Two new tests in `mod watcher_tests`; both call the private production function `attempt_of(&job, resumed, unlanded)` (scope_guard.rs:580), which is reachable from the in-module test.

Test 1 `attempt_of_records_how_far_a_near_complete_rejection_got`: `rig(1.0, 0.8, &[Some(0)])`, `r.ask`, `r.go` (Rejected), then clone the job from `r.records().jobs`.
- `attempt_of(&job, false, false)` gives verdict Rejected and `progress == Some(Progress { met: 1, total: 2, bounded: true })`.
- Set `verification` to None: progress None.
- Set `outcome.state` to Failed with reason `the producer returned no valid report`: verdict Failed, progress None, though the verification is still present.
- Set `outcome.state` to Failed with the real `crate::disk::LowDisk { free, required }.text()` as in scope_guard.rs:2337-2341: verdict Environment, progress None.
- Set `outcome.state` to Landed: Accepted, progress None.

Test 2 `near_complete_gap_is_bounded_only_by_findings_of_the_gap` (finding 1) overwrites `verification.criteria`, `.findings` and `.agent_verdict` on the cloned rejected job with the output of the real `crate::verify::judge(&VerdictInputs { .. })`. It is fed `VerdictOutput`, `CriterionVerdictOutput` and `FindingOutput` literals (athena_context::outputs, outputs.rs:245-300). The rest of `VerdictInputs` is empty or None, and `map_base` and `map_candidate` are set only in case (b). Cases, each checked by `attempt_of(..).progress` and `near_complete`:
- 9 content criteria, 8 met, no findings: 8 of 9, bounded, near_complete true.
- The same plus one verifier Major on the gap: bounded.
- The same plus two verifier Majors: unbounded.
- (a, critic case) 9 criteria of which one is Behavior, unmet, citing a command that was not seen running, plus a verifier Major and the Athena Major that judge adds: two Majors for one gap, bounded.
- (b, critic case) 9 content criteria, 8 met, commands verified, plus one Athena Major from `map_base` `| A1-1 | x | Open |` and `map_candidate` `| A1-1 | x | Covered |` (verify.rs:249-290): unbounded.
- An unassessed criterion (the output lists 8 of 9 criteria): bounded, with its single Athena Major covered by `judged_gaps`.
- A verifier Blocker: unbounded.
- `request_misread` true in the output: unbounded.
- `agent_verdict` None: unbounded.
- The verifier invocation's `outcome` set to Killed in the clone: unbounded. Its `seq` removed from `job.invocations`: unbounded.
- A `CheckRun` with passed false and no note (built field by field as in status.rs:2662-2675): unbounded. With a note starting `PRE_EXISTING_NOTE`: bounded again.
